survey: A stage spotlight hangs from a steel truss. The truss crosses the top of the frame and is seen slightly from below, with its tubes and diagonal braces receding in a consistent way. A dark clamp block grips the lower truss tube, and a short stem drops from it to the top bar of a rectangular yoke. The yoke's two arms come down on either side of the cylindrical lamp can. A grey pivot knob on the right arm meets the can's side; the left pivot is hidden behind the can. The can tilts down and toward the viewer, to the lower left, and its rounded back end shows to the right of the yoke. The front has a thick flared rim, drawn as a tilted ellipse, and inside it are three round LED lenses (yellow, cyan, red) lying flat in the face plate. Their foreshortening matches the rim's angle. The truss, yoke, can and rim all read as one low camera looking slightly up. The can's sides narrow toward the back, which is the right direction for its tilt. There is no ground plane, and the hanging contact (clamp on tube, yoke on pivots) is drawn believably.
